meta.title: Primordial Paradox recipes: jrpg scope (Final Fantasy I to III, Dragon Quest I to IV, Mother, Crystalis)
meta.author: job-discovery
meta.chip: NES 2A03 (pulse1, pulse2, triangle, noise, DPCM) plus Konami VRC6 (vrc6_p1, vrc6_p2, vrc6_saw)
meta.reference_rule: study only; no melody transcribed, copied or reconstructed from these rows
meta.param_types: numbers are JSON numbers, channel and enum values are strings; params_text is the same content as one line for the arranger prompt
meta.corpus_caveat: the two statistics files are normalised to 120 bpm and 4/4, so no recipe takes tempo or metre from them; tempo and metre come from published analyses and are cited per recipe

recipes.name: Octave punctuation
recipes.rule: Place one leap of exactly an octave in each 2 to 4 bar phrase, on a strong beat, and bring the line back inside the phrase's range within two beats. The octave is the phrase's punctuation mark and the cheapest identity device the chip has.
recipes.params_text: octave_leaps_per_phrase=1; interval_semitones=12; place_on=strong_beat; return_within_beats=2; hold_frames_after_leap=3
forbidden: two octave leaps inside one phrase
an octave leap on the last note of the hook
an octave leap on the triangle bass, which reads as a mistake
recipes.evidence: measured: 5.39 percent of Uematsu melody intervals are up 12 semitones and 2.75 percent down 12; the two most common two-interval windows in the corpus are octave up then back (262) and octave down then back (248), together 4.7 percent of all windows

recipes.name: Dotted sixteenth lurch
recipes.rule: Build the cell from sixteenths and favour the dotted eighth over the plain eighth, so the line lurches forward instead of gliding. Keep the leading sixteenth short and put the long value across the beat.
recipes.params_text: subdivision=16ths; sixteenth_share_pct=60; dotted_eighth_share_pct=12; plain_eighth_share_pct=11; accent=long_value_after_short
forbidden: dotted rhythms in every bar, which flattens the contrast
a dotted figure on the bass under a sixteenth melody
swing feel applied on top of dotted sixteenths
recipes.evidence: measured: melody duration histogram in sixteenths is 59.6 percent for 1, 12.4 percent for 3, 11.4 percent for 2, and the commonest pair is sixteenth plus sixteenth (5665 windows)

recipes.name: Narrow battle riff over rich harmony
recipes.rule: Keep the battle melody inside 12 semitones and let the harmony do the work. Write two to four repeated notes, one step, and a fixed rhythmic cell that survives the whole cue, while the chords move under it.
recipes.params_text: melody_range_max_semitones=12; beats_per_note=0.88; repeated_notes_min=2; chord_changes_per_bar=2; tempo_bpm=150; meter=4/4
forbidden: a wide, singable battle melody
one chord per bar
a melody that changes direction every beat
recipes.evidence: published: FF I Battle is G minor at 150 bpm with an 8 semitone range, 0.88 beats per note over 106 beats, 80 percent diatonic, 69 percent chord tones, chord complexity 94 against an average of 50

recipes.name: Two voice broken chord cue
recipes.rule: Write the whole cue as one broken chord pattern on pulse1 and its delayed twin on pulse2, with no drums, no bass and no melody. The figure has to be interesting enough to loop for a minute without help.
recipes.params_text: voices=2; pattern=up_then_down_over_two_octaves; subdivision=16ths; delay_eighths=1; vol_pct_second=40; drums=none; triangle=unused
forbidden: adding a bass to rescue a weak arpeggio
a drum layer in a two voice cue
changing the pattern mid cue, which removes the only identity the cue has
recipes.evidence: published: B flat major, 100 bpm, one arpeggio pattern, melodic complexity 93 to 94, progression novelty 95; measured: the Prelude is 19 bars and the only two voice cue in the FF I corpus

recipes.name: Delayed detuned twin
recipes.rule: Double the lead on the second pulse, a few cents flat and a fraction of a beat late, at reduced volume. The pair reads as one expressive instrument rather than two square waves.
recipes.params_text: cents_offset=-8; delay_ms=18; vol_pct=70; envelope=soft_decay; channel_pair=pulse1+pulse2
forbidden: detuning the bass
three voices all detuned at once, which reads as a mistake rather than an ensemble
detuning a staccato sixteenth line, where the delay is inaudible
recipes.evidence: published in his own words: the same line on two pulses with the second shifted in pitch and time makes plain electronic tones feel emotional; and the Prelude is described as two pulses with the second about an eighth late

recipes.name: Three voice town warmth
recipes.lineage: Uematsu, FF I to III towns
recipes.rule: Melody on pulse1 at 25 percent duty, a horn pair or a light arpeggio on pulse2, walking bass on the triangle, and at most a soft noise rim. Warmth comes from the duty and from the number of notes per bar, not from added voices.
recipes.params_text: voices=3; lead_duty=0.25; notes_per_bar=5.3; bass=walking; bass_beats_per_note=1.0; noise=soft_rim_every_other_bar; tempo_bpm_min=100; tempo_bpm_max=132
forbidden: eighth note driving bass in a town cue
lead duty below 0.25, which reads as thin and cold
a full drum kit under a town cue
recipes.evidence: measured: median 5.3 melody notes per bar and 0.66 beats per note in the Uematsu corpus, median three voices per piece; published: FF I Town is C major, 11 bars, FF II Town 24 bars, FF III Town of Water 28 bars

recipes.name: Event sting, two to three bars
recipes.rule: End the sting before the listener can predict it: two or three bars, no loop, last note held on the tonic. A sting that reaches a full cadence in the middle has already failed.
recipes.params_text: bars_min=2; bars_max=3; loop=false; final_note=held_tonic; voices_max=3; drums=one_hit
forbidden: a drum fill in a sting
an arpeggio run of more than one octave
a sting that ends on the dominant
recipes.evidence: measured: FF I Fanfare 2 bars (G major), Save Jingle 3 bars (A major), FF III Item Get 2 bars (F major), A Comrade Joins 3 bars, Garuda Defeated 3 bars, Rest at the Inn 3 bars; Mother Fanfare 2 bars, Sleep 2 bars, Level Up 3 bars

recipes.name: Victory cadence a third away
recipes.lineage: Uematsu victory and level up cues
recipes.rule: Write the victory six to eight bars, put its key a third away from the battle key on the flat side, and close with a full authentic cadence. This is the one sting allowed a drum fill and a crash, and the only one that does not loop.
recipes.params_text: bars_min=6; bars_max=8; key_relation_to_battle=minor_third_down_or_minor_sixth_up; cadence=authentic; drums=fanfare_crash_on_last_bar; loop=false
forbidden: the victory in the battle's own key, which sounds like a continuation
a half cadence anywhere in a victory
reusing the battle melody with new words, which reads as a remix
recipes.evidence: measured: FF I Battle is G minor and FF I Victory is E flat major over 8 bars, a minor sixth up from the battle tonic; Mother Victory is one bar in C major and Level Up three bars in E flat major

recipes.name: Inner voice in thirds below the lead
recipes.rule: Give the second pulse a line that runs a third to a sixth below the lead, moving slower than the lead and never crossing it in the same rhythm. This fills the texture without spending a melody.
recipes.params_text: interval_below=third_or_fourth_or_sixth; inner_median_pitch_midi=62; inner_beats_per_note=0.47; same_rhythm_as_lead=false; register=below_lead_above_bass
forbidden: the inner voice in unison with the lead for more than two bars
a parallel third line for a whole cue, which sounds like an exercise
the inner voice louder than 70 percent of the lead
recipes.evidence: measured: the Uematsu corpus has 183 inner voice roles against 104 melody roles, with a median inner pitch of MIDI 62 and 0.47 beats per note, so the inner line moves faster and sits a ninth below the lead

recipes.name: Horn fifth pair
recipes.rule: Write the two upper voices as a horn pair: one moves by step while the other holds or steps inside the chord tones, arriving on a perfect fifth or sixth, and repeat the figure in a mirrored pair. This is the texture of a brass section on two pulse channels.
recipes.params_text: voices_in_pair=2; arrival_intervals=fifth_or_sixth; upper_moves=by_step; lower_moves=chord_tones; pair_repeats=2; duty_upper=0.25; duty_lower=0.5
forbidden: parallel fifths for three consecutive moves without a step in the upper voice
a fourth voice attempting the same texture
the pair played on the triangle and the noise channel
recipes.evidence: published: the Overture introduction is built on exchanges between horns and trumpets in horn fifths; horn fifths are the acceptable case of hidden fifths where the top voice moves by step, and they come in pairs

recipes.name: Maestoso fanfare frame
recipes.rule: Open with two to four bars of fanfare at a stately tempo, building voice by voice: one pulse alone, then the horn pair, then the bass, then a noise crash on the arrival. The frame exists to be recognised in the first two bars.
recipes.params_text: bars=4; tempo_bpm_min=100; tempo_bpm_max=110; entry_order=pulse1_then_pulse2_then_triangle_then_noise; bars_between_entries=1; arrival=tonic_with_crash; marking=maestoso
forbidden: a drum groove inside the fanfare
starting with a full texture
more than four bars before the march arrives
recipes.evidence: published: the Overture has three sections, a majestic fanfare marked Maestoso, a march main theme, and a quiet passage into a Piu Lento close; the fanfare is where the horn and trumpet exchanges live

recipes.name: March main section with snare
recipes.rule: Write the main section as a march: steady quarters in the melody, root on every beat on the triangle, and a snare figure on the noise channel that plays a short roll into each phrase start. The snare is what makes it a march.
recipes.params_text: meter=4/4; tempo_bpm=120; bass=root_per_beat; melody_durations=quarters_and_eighths; snare=noise_mid_rate; snare_roll=one_beat_before_phrase; bars=16
forbidden: a march with no snare
syncopated bass under a march melody
sixteenth note runs longer than one beat
recipes.evidence: published: the main section adds a lively snare drum rhythm that gives it the character of a march, and marches were chosen as a natural fit for the opening of an RPG

recipes.name: Quiet passage into a slower close
recipes.rule: Before the last two bars, drop to one voice and one or two bars of near silence, then close slower than the rest of the cue. The sudden quiet is the drama, and the slower close is the resolution.
recipes.params_text: quiet_bars=2; voices_in_quiet=1; tempo_drop_pct=15; final_hold_bars=2; marking=piu_lento; drums=none_in_quiet
forbidden: the quiet passage held for more than two bars
a fade instead of a tempo drop
a new melody in the quiet passage
recipes.evidence: published: the ending begins with a sudden quiet passage and then a slower conclusion marked Piu Lento, and the melodic string passage leads into a lavish close

recipes.name: Classical cadence over a walking bass
recipes.rule: Give every four or eight bar phrase a real cadence, with the bass walking in step motion into the cadence chord and an approach note on the last beat. Chord changes run one per beat to one per two beats.
recipes.params_text: phrase_bars=8; cadence=authentic_or_half_alternating; bass=walking_step_motion; approach_note=last_beat_of_phrase; chord_changes_per_bar=2; melody_durations=quarters_and_eighths
forbidden: a phrase with no cadence
a bass pedal under a cadence
a cadence on every two bars, which turns the cue into a jingle
recipes.evidence: published: he wrote game music as drama music, with the grammar of the common practice period, on the logic that an RPG is a kind of drama; measured: chord changes per bar 3.94 in the Uematsu corpus and 3.55 in the Mother corpus show how fast harmony moves in the genre

recipes.name: Fixed identity piece, reorchestrated
recipes.rule: Write one short identity piece and never rewrite it. When the game or the act changes, change the instrumentation, the register and the drum weight only. The melody is a logo.
recipes.params_text: melody=fixed; changes_allowed=instrumentation_register_drum_weight_tempo_pct_10; length_bars=16; reuse=every_act_or_sequel; rewrites=0
forbidden: changing notes between versions
reharmonising the identity piece, which breaks the recognition
adding a new section to it
recipes.evidence: published: every Dragon Quest entry he scored carries a nearly identical upbeat Overture, across more than 500 pieces and 35 years

recipes.name: Middle section to the dominant or relative key
recipes.rule: At bar 9 or 17, move the middle section to the dominant or the relative major, then return. One key change per loop, at a section boundary, with the same rhythmic cell continuing underneath.
recipes.params_text: change_at_bar=9_or_17; targets=dominant_or_relative_major_or_relative_minor; keys_per_loop_max=2; rhythm_cell=unchanged; return=by_bar_17_or_25
forbidden: a key change inside a phrase
more than two keys in one loop
two key changes in the same loop
recipes.evidence: published: FF II's main piece is described as Baroque in shape building to a fanfare; the Kirby two section model is a move to the parallel minor at the section boundary; measured: chord progression novelty 88 against 50 average for the Kid Icarus 6/8 cue shows how far the genre will move harmonically

recipes.name: Orchestra inside three voices
recipes.rule: With three voices, write two as a brass or horn pair and one as the bass. Do not attempt a four note chord, do not arpeggiate to fake it in a march, and let the ear supply the missing third or root.
recipes.params_text: voices=3; pair=upper_two; bass=triangle_root_and_fifth_only; four_note_chords=false; arpeggio_in_march=false; implied_root=true
forbidden: two voices doubling at the octave through a whole phrase
arpeggiating a chord in a march, which breaks the march rhythm
a seventh chord stated in three voices in a slow fanfare
recipes.evidence: published in his own words: a real professional should be able to write music with three voices only, in his head he hears a whole orchestra inside two or three sounds, and in the opening theme he hears horns very clearly, because he sang three part choir

recipes.name: Repeated note melody
recipes.rule: Build the tune from one pitch repeated on the beat, then one step away and back. The repeat is the tune: it carries the pulse so the harmony can stay plain.
recipes.params_text: repeat_share_pct=16; repeat_count_min=3; step_away_max_semitones=2; range_max_semitones=12; notes_per_bar=4.66; envelope_on_repeat=re_trigger_volume_nibble
forbidden: a repeated note at the same volume for every repeat
an octave leap in a repeated note phrase
a repeat held for a full bar
recipes.evidence: measured: 16.2 percent of Tanaka corpus melody intervals are zero against 6.0 percent for Uematsu, and step plus repeat motion is 61.8 percent of all intervals against 49.2 percent

recipes.name: One finger singable theme
recipes.rule: Write the theme so a child can play it with one finger: no leap larger than a fourth, one octave of range, one chromatic note at most, and a rhythm a beginner can count. No cadence is required, so it can stop anywhere.
recipes.params_text: max_leap_semitones=5; range_max_semitones=12; chromatic_notes_max=1; stepwise=true; rhythm=quarters_and_eighths_with_one_dotted_pair; cadence_required=false
forbidden: an octave leap in a one finger theme
a melody that needs the harmony to make sense
a dominant seventh cadence at the end
recipes.evidence: published: Itoi asked for a song anyone could hum along with, imagined a child who cannot really play the piano playing it with a single finger; measured: Tanaka median range 22.5 semitones, leaps over 19 semitones 0.58 percent

recipes.name: Suspended chord held over the tonic
recipes.lineage: Suzuki and Tanaka, the playful strange
recipes.rule: Hold a fourth over the tonic triad for a full bar and do not resolve it. The chord never becomes a dominant, so the cue sounds unresolved in a friendly way, which is the Mother brand of strange.
recipes.params_text: chord=Isus4; hold_bars=1; resolution=none; sus4_share_pct=22; melody=diatonic_chord_tones
forbidden: resolving the suspension to the third in the same bar
two suspensions in consecutive bars
a suspended chord in a battle cue, where tension must be functional
recipes.evidence: measured: sus4 is 21.8 percent of chord changes in the Tanaka corpus, the second largest category after plain major, while diminished 7 is 0.2 percent

recipes.name: One flat key cue per game
recipes.rule: Most cues sit in common keys. Give one cue per game a flat key that no other cue uses, such as A flat major or D flat major, and keep its texture plain so the key is the strangeness.
recipes.params_text: flat_key_share_pct=12; examples=Ab_major_Db_major_Gb_major_F_minor; texture=plain_three_voice; tempo_bpm=120
forbidden: two flat key cues in the same act
a flat key cue with a full drum kit
a flat key that is used for the battle music
recipes.evidence: measured: 29 major against 11 minor in the Mother corpus, with A flat major three times in 40 pieces and D flat, F minor, E flat major once each, so the odd keys are rare and specific

recipes.name: One genre per location
recipes.lineage: Suzuki and Tanaka, the disorderly spread
recipes.rule: Give each location its own genre reference (jazz, lullaby, march, surf, waltz) and keep only the melodic language shared across locations. The spread of styles is the world design, not an inconsistency.
recipes.params_text: genres_per_score_min=5; shared_across_locations=melodic_language_and_lead_timbre; changed_per_location=groove_drum_kit_bass_type_tempo; reuse_recurring_theme=across_acts
forbidden: the same drum kit in every location
one genre stretched across the whole game
a location genre that contradicts the melodic language of the score
recipes.evidence: published: Itoi credits Suzuki and Tanaka with a broad, disorderly spread of styles, says EarthBound carried more jazzy pieces than Mother, and names the first use of vibrato in a game soundtrack

recipes.name: Slow pedal under a stepwise tune
recipes.rule: Put one bass note per bar, or one per two bars, low on the triangle, and let the melody do the moving. A slow pedal leaves the listener free to hear a plain tune.
recipes.params_text: bass_beats_per_note=2.0; bass_median_pitch_midi=44; bass_changes_per_bar=0.5; melody=stepwise; drums=none_or_one_hit_per_bar
forbidden: a walking bass under a stepwise tune
pedal bass with a syncopated melody in the same register
pedal bass on the pulse channel
recipes.evidence: measured: Tanaka bass median pitch is MIDI 44 with 0.445 beats per note, lower and longer than the Uematsu bass at MIDI 48 and 0.364 beats per note

recipes.name: Blue third with late vibrato
recipes.rule: Bend the third of a major chord down toward the blue third on its long note, and add vibrato after the attack rather than at it. One bend per phrase, on the longest note.
recipes.params_text: bend_interval=major_third_down_to_blue_third; bend_cents=40; bend_time_frames=6; vibrato_start_frames_after_attack=3; vibrato_depth_cents=15; vibrato_rate_hz=5; register_byte=low_only
forbidden: vibrato on every note
writing the high period byte for vibrato, which resets phase and pops
a bend on the bass
recipes.evidence: published: Itoi says EarthBound was the first game soundtrack with vibrato or string bending and carried more jazzy pieces; chip: vibrato must go through the low period byte or the phase resets and pops

recipes.name: One bar victory, three bar level up
recipes.rule: Compress the reward to its minimum: one bar for a battle win, three bars for a level up, each ending on a held tonic. Anything longer competes with the next screen.
recipes.params_text: victory_bars=1; level_up_bars=3; final_note=held_tonic; voices_max=3; loop=false; key=bright_major
forbidden: a victory over four bars
a drum fill in a one bar sting
a level up sting that changes key halfway
recipes.evidence: measured: Mother Victory is 1 bar in C major, Fanfare 1 is 1 bar in C major, Level Up is 3 bars in E flat major, Sleep is 2 bars in B flat major

recipes.name: Waltz with root and two stabs
recipes.rule: In 3/4, put the root on beat 1 on the triangle and the chord on beats 2 and 3, either as a saw stab or a two note pulse dyad, and let the melody breathe on beat 1. A waltz is a slow cue with a fast accompaniment.
recipes.params_text: meter=3/4; tempo_bpm_min=100; tempo_bpm_max=120; bass=root_on_beat_1; chord_stabs=beats_2_and_3; stab_channel=vrc6_saw; saw_rate_max=40; melody_on=beat_1; seventh_chord_most_used=flat_seven
forbidden: a drum backbeat in 3/4
sixteenth note stabs, which the saw accumulator cannot reset
a four bar waltz phrase that never lands on beat 1
recipes.evidence: published: the Final Fantasy victory fanfare lineage is in 3/4 at 107 bpm with the flat seven as its most used chord and chord complexity 100; chip: saw accumulator rates above 42 distort

recipes.name: 6/8 travel cue
recipes.rule: In 6/8, put the bass on groups 1 and 4 only and let the melody skip across the three eighth groups. The metre, not the melody, does the identifying.
recipes.params_text: meter=6/8; tempo_bpm=152; bass_hits=groups_1_and_4; melody_grouping=across_the_beat; drums=shaker_on_every_eighth_or_none; progression_novelty=high
forbidden: bass on every eighth, which turns 6/8 into 3/4
a straight eighth melody that erases the compound feel
a 6/8 cue with a march snare
recipes.evidence: published: Kid Icarus Underworld is 152 bpm in 6/8 with a 22 semitone range and chord progression novelty 88 against an average of 50

recipes.name: Driving eighth bass and noise backbeat
recipes.rule: Run the triangle on one root per eighth with no rests, put the noise snare on beats 2 and 4, and keep a two bar riff cell on pulse1 that repeats with one operation every third statement.
recipes.params_text: bass=eighth_notes_root_only; bass_beats_per_note=0.5; snare=noise_mid_rate_on_2_and_4; kick=dpcm_on_1_and_3; riff_cell_bars=2; operations_every=3; tempo_bpm_min=140; tempo_bpm_max=160
forbidden: a bass rest in a battle cue
the same riff cell five times with no operation
a tom fill in a two bar riff
recipes.evidence: measured: Uematsu bass median duration is 0.364 beats per note, the fastest of the two corpora; published: battle cues sit at 150 bpm in 4/4 (FF I Battle); chip: noise and DPCM are the cheap kick and snare pair

recipes.name: Dungeon tick with no snare
recipes.rule: Remove the snare. Give the noise channel one periodic mode tick per bar, keep the triangle on a slow pedal, and let the melody sit low and sparse. A dungeon cue is defined by what it removes.
recipes.params_text: snare=none; noise=periodic_mode_tick_per_bar; bass=slow_pedal; note_density_per_bar_max=4; melody_register=low; tempo_bpm_min=90; tempo_bpm_max=120
forbidden: a backbeat snare in a dungeon
a bright lead duty with a fast line
a drum fill into the loop point
recipes.evidence: chip: periodic mode shortens the LFSR sequence so the noise reads as a metallic tick rather than a hit; measured: FF I Dungeon is 12 bars in C minor, FF III The Dungeon 16 bars in F minor, Mother Cave 23 bars in A minor at a median 4.66 notes per bar

recipes.name: Changed ending that points back to bar one
recipes.rule: Write the last two beats of the loop so they lead into the first note of bar 1, and change that ending on every second repeat, either by a deceptive cadence or by rewriting the last two notes. The seam is where a 16 bar loop is won or lost.
recipes.params_text: seam_bars=2; endings=2; alternate_endings=true; exact_repeats_max=2; deceptive_cadence_on_repeat=true; loop_bars=16_or_8_or_24
forbidden: a last bar identical to the first bar in every voice
more than two exact repeats in a row
an ending that resolves so strongly that the loop restart sounds like an edit
recipes.evidence: published: varied repetition is preferred to literal at 2.7 to 1, and the Kirby model rewrites the repeat ending as a deceptive cadence into the relative minor; measured: 16 bars is the workhorse loop length in both corpora
